answer: Persistent Fault Beacon. Each identity carries a signed history of resolved disputes; when a dispute resolves against it, the operator's master key emits a beacon flagging every identity derived from it. A single ember of unresolved fault blocks all linked identities from new contracts until cleared. Attacker cost: losing one identity taints the whole cluster, so each fake identity forfeits the operator's accumulated reputation signal and future revenue, not just its own deposit.
